messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: sudden 429 spike detected on production ingress — 10m rolling error rate 21% (baseline 0.3%). Top affected routes: /v1/chat/stream, /v1/embeddings. Top origin tenants: tenant-acmehealth, tenant-startupx. Auto-escalation threshold exceeded. Paging oncall.
jamie: acked. I'm on it. grabbing dashboard now — @kevin if you can join that'd be great. ETA 2m.
kevin: on my way. looking at the top-ten offending tenants. I see a heavy tail of requests with large context lengths and repeated retries from tenant-acmehealth. 429s are hitting our edge gateway queues, not the model workers yet.
jamie: good call. can we apply a short-term per-tenant QPS cap to the top 5 offenders and reduce burst allowance? propose: tenant_qps cap = 6 -> 2 for 5m, burst_tokens 50 -> 10. that'll buy time without dropping sessions entirely.
priya: I can flip the rate-limiter policy in the control plane. patch config name: "rl/tenant-emergency/2026-03-15". doing a dry-run against staging then promote. curl to change:

```
curl -X POST https://internal-control.redwood/api/v1/rate-limits \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  -d '{"tenant_id":"tenant-acmehealth","qps":2,"burst":10,"ttl_seconds":300}'
```
jamie: sounds good. also let's temporarily disable the experimental "burst-allow" feature flag for embeddings — we've seen cache invalidation causing amplified retries.
kevin: agreed. disabling flag now -> `featureflag service:embeddings:burst-allow = false`
ops-bot: feature flag change recorded: embeddings.burst-allow = false by kevin (runbook ref: RB-433). link: https://internal-control/flags/embeddings/burst-allow
priya: pushing rl config to prod in 3...2...1... done. response: 200. policy id rl-20260315-1
liz: support FYI — I'm drafting a short customer-facing note to affected customers (AcmeHealth and StartupX) to let them know we throttled heavy clients to protect platform stability. tagging account owners.
jamie: monitoring dashboards — spike amplitude dropped within 90s of policy flip. 429 rate now 2.6% down from 21%. CPU on model workers stable. latency tail improved.
kevin: can confirm queue depth at edge reduced, worker backpressure cleared. posting quick snippet from the timeline logs:
```
[1738204590] ingress queue depth 142 -> 24
[1738204620] 429 rate 21% -> 3.1%
[1738204660] worker p95 latency 420ms -> 190ms
```
jamie: thumbs. @liz please let support ops know we may need to follow up with AcmeHealth on SDK retry behavior (they're retrying on 429s without backoff).
liz: noted. message drafted and queued for the account manager. will include suggested SDK backoff guidance and offer a 1:1 troubleshooting call.
kevin: small wrinkle — a secondary tenant (tenant-startupx) is approaching cap and started failing model-side auth checks due to malformed tokens. can we relax auth error logging to avoid logging flood? maybe set auth_log_rate = 1/s for that tenant.
priya: sure. lowering auth log rate for tenant-startupx to 1/s now.
ops-bot: config change recorded: logging.auth_rate_limit applied for tenant-startupx (by priya).
jamie: quick sanity — can we open a short window for whitelisted latency-sensitive customers to bypass the QPS cap? AcmeHealth is whitelisted for critical endpoints, but their retries are the problem. Suggest adding a pathway: bypass only with strict token that expires in 10m.
kevin: ok will create temporary token allowlist for 10 mins. creating token: `allow-1738-acme-10m` and injecting into control plane.
ops-bot: allowlist entry created: allow-1738-acme-10m (expires 1738205167)
jamie: good. effect on metrics: ACME telemetry shows sessions continue for high-priority keys but overall 429s remain suppressed. moving to stabilization.
kevin: leaving a short checklist for follow-up:
- run a prompt set against embeddings to validate no quality regressions
- review retry behavior in SDKs for top 3 offenders
- consider permanent baseline qps caps for noisy tenants
- write post-incident note with timeline

jamie: I'm going to hand off to kevin — my shift ends in 6m. kevin you'll take post-mitigation lead and coordinate with support for customer comms?
kevin: will do. I'll keep this thread updated and post final metrics once steady for 15m. thanks team.
liz: posting customer notes now, will include a link to status page update.
incident-bot: Incident annotated: MITIGATION_APPLIED, incident_id INC-20260315-77, severity: medium, current_state: stabilizing. next: oncall handoff recorded (jamie -> kevin).
jamie: :wave: handing off. kevin — ping me if anything spikes, otherwise I'll pick this up tomorrow morning for the postmortem.
kevin: thx. monitoring alert thresholds adjusted to avoid noisy paging during cooldown: 429 alert threshold raised to 5% for 10m window. will revert after 30m stable.
jamie: :thumbsup: closing my side. good job everyone.
kevin: final snapshot before I close the incident in 30m: 429 rate 0.9%, p95 latency 180ms, queue depth 12. will archive logs and link in the postmortem.
ops-bot: incident INC-20260315-77 state updated to stabilizing; ticket INC-20260315-77 created in ops tracker.
